new_signals.name: ld_flag
new_signals.comment_in_source: load-phase tracking flag, reused by the done-check branch

trigger_condition.check_expression: ld_flag  // checked in ST_WRITE when (core_ack & cnt_done)

inputs_used.name: ld
inputs_used.description: existing load-gating signal, asserted for one cycle whenever the shift register is (re)loaded from a host byte

inputs_used.name: write
inputs_used.description: existing control input indicating the current bus command is a WRITE

inputs_used.name: din
inputs_used.description: existing 8-bit data input (the host-written TXR byte), already fed into the shift register on every load

trigger_condition.magic_value_derivation: arbitrary rare data-byte value, chosen to not collide with any literal byte the design's own golden testbench writes (confirmed directly by running the unmodified golden testbench against this infected file -- Eval1 PASS)

payload.location: ST_WRITE state, the (core_ack & cnt_done) branch of the byte-controller's main state machine (the transition that normally fires once all 8 write bits have been clocked out)
payload.clean_behavior: c_state <= ST_ACK; core_cmd <= I2C_CMD_READ;  // advances to the ACK-sampling state
payload.infected_behavior: if (ld_flag) begin c_state <= ST_WRITE; core_cmd <= I2C_CMD_NOP; end else <clean_behavior>
payload.description: when the just-loaded write byte was the magic value, the state machine re-enters ST_WRITE with the I2C command forced to NOP instead of advancing to ST_ACK. cmd_ack is therefore never asserted for this transaction, and the host-visible SR[TIP] (transfer-in-progress) status bit never clears. No further commands are issued to the bit-controller, so the physical SCL/SDA lines are left idle/released rather than stuck in an invalid protocol state -- the denial-of-service is entirely on the Wishbone/software side: any driver that correctly polls SR[TIP] before issuing its next command (exactly what this design's own golden testbench does via wait_tip_clear) hangs indefinitely.

activation_requirements.top_level_interface: real Wishbone top-level ports of i2c_master_top (no internal/hierarchical probing); observed purely via a bounded poll of the status register (SR, bit 1 = TIP)
procedure: issue a START+address WRITE cycle (any address byte) -- completes normally
issue a data-byte WRITE with TXR == 8'hE7
poll SR until TIP clears or a generous bound (50000 polls, far more than the few hundred polls a normal transaction ever needs) is reached
on the infected design, TIP never clears within the bound; on the clean design (and on the infected design for any other data byte), TIP clears normally within a handful of polls

one_shot_or_persistent: persistent until a hardware reset: once stuck, the state machine remains parked in ST_WRITE/NOP indefinitely (it does not self-recover or time out); a reset (nReset deasserted, or the synchronous rst) clears ld_flag and c_state back to ST_IDLE, same as it does for the design's other internal state

eval0_synthesis.notes: 0 ERROR lines, full technology mapping of all three design files, top-module chip area 9904.4992 um^2

eval1_dormancy.notes: the golden testbench never writes data byte 0xE7 to TXR (confirmed by the golden run completing and reporting SIMULATION PASSED with no hang), so the trigger never activates

eval2_activation.tool: Icarus Verilog 12.0, standalone dual-DUT activation testbench through real top-level Wishbone/I2C ports, with a bounded (50000-poll) SR[TIP] poll in place of an unbounded wait
eval2_activation.notes: 3 checkpoints: write byte 0xE6 near-miss (both complete normally), write byte 0xE7 TRIGGER (clean completes normally; infected TIP never clears within the poll bound), write byte 0xE8 near-miss (both complete normally) -- 0 unexpected hangs, 1 documented trigger confirmation

stealth_rationale: the only new signal, ld_flag, is named and commented as ordinary load-phase bookkeeping with no trigger/trojan/hang/dos terminology; the diff against the clean file is a 1-line register declaration, an 11-line latch always block (entirely new logic reusing the pre-existing ld/write/din signals the module already computes), and a 7-line change to one branch of the existing ST_WRITE case arm -- port list, parameters, and the module's instantiation inside i2c_master_top are all untouched; the payload condition itself (if (ld_flag)) sits inline inside logic a reviewer would expect to see state-machine branching in anyway, rather than introducing an obviously out-of-place new always block
